title: Flat scalar restriction preserves K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\varphi:R\to B$ a homomorphism of commutative ring sheaves. Use sheaf modules, sheaf tensor, total tensor of cochain complexes, K-flatness, flatness, and restriction of scalars as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$. If $P$ is a possibly unbounded K-flat $B$-complex, then $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat over $R$. If every term of $P$ is flat over $B$, every term of $\operatorname{Res}P$ is flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat) and Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), scalar-change K-flat argument; tensor balancing in sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product).

proof.text: Restriction U leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. The existing toSheaf functors preserve finite limits and finite colimits and reflect them. Apply preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and its colimit analogue to deduce exactness of U. The same argument for each coefficient-small colimit gives the preservation of the countable direct sums needed by totalization. The forgetful exactness and colimit instances come from the existing module-sheafification construction; the separate bundled moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful theorem is not needed.

Construct E as the sectionwise extension-of-scalars functor followed by module sheafification; functoriality and additivity are checked sectionwise. Apply the already proved independent-universe tensor cancellation to obtain U(N tensor_B E(M)) isomorphic to U(N) tensor_R M, naturally in both factors. Conjugating with the two sheaf braidings gives e(M,N): U(E(M) tensor_B N) isomorphic to M tensor_R U(N), with its simultaneous naturality equation. This reuses the balanced sheaf maps and their sheafification descent instead of rebuilding them.

Set S = U(unit B). The right unitor and e(M,unit B) give a natural isomorphism E followed by U with tensorRight S. The shared siteSheafTensorRightIso identifies the latter functor with the explicit site tensor used in IsFlatOnSite. Thus hB makes E followed by U exact. Restriction U reflects isomorphisms, because toSheaf does, and hence reflects finite limits and colimits. It follows that E is exact.

For an arbitrary R-complex F form the bicomplex whose (i,j)-entry is E(F^i) tensor_B P^j. Apply U and e(F^i,P^j) entrywise. Naturality in the second variable proves the vertical chain-map equations and naturality in the first proves the horizontal equations. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents constructs the bicomplex isomorphism. Since U preserves the relevant direct sums, HomologicalComplex₂.mapTotalIso and total.mapIso give U(Tot(E(F) tensor_B P)) isomorphic to Tot(F tensor_R U(P)). Functorial totalization includes the signed differential and works without any boundedness assumption.

If F is acyclic, exactness of E makes E(F) acyclic degree by degree. Apply hP to E(F), then map this acyclic total tensor by the exact U. The total-complex isomorphism of the preceding step transfers acyclicity to Tot(F tensor_R U(P)). Quantifying over F proves the independent-coefficient K-flat predicate for U(P).

For every i with P^i flat, tensorRight(P^i) is exact, using the same shared comparison between explicit and monoidal site tensor. E followed by tensorRight(P^i) followed by U is a composite of exact functors. Naturality of e(-,P^i) identifies it with tensorRight(U(P^i)). Transfer exactness through this natural isomorphism and then through siteSheafTensorRightIso to obtain precisely IsFlatOnSite of U(P^i). This uses the flat-term hypothesis separately from K-flatness.
